data.body:
COMPLETE. Both mechanisms are on main, and the sweep they enable is now safe to actually run.

## What landed, in order

| change | merged | what |
|---|---|---|
| 1702 | 04b78f5e7e | compaction OFF the close path (the original P0 — a 13m53s lock hold) |
| 1717 | e0a55d5fac | scheduled sweep, the amortized path where CI exists |
| 1727 | d2dea317ec | operation-linked trigger, the floor for stores with no CI and no cron |
| 1733 | 2af5a4c773 | fix-forward for the four defects that rode in on the stale 1727 |
| 1739 | 50cc45f0d1 | one history walk per sweep, hoisted out of the lock; scoped staging; re-yield |

The peer's 1732 (ea6ee67e6a) fixed the fifth stale-1727 defect, `_config_schema.py` over the
800-LOC cap — never mine, and the thing that blocked 1733's CI until it landed.

## The operator constraint is satisfied

"compaction needs to work in environments without local cron and CI." It does: a close triggers
compaction without performing it, via two O(1) checks and a detached worker, so an adopter with
neither still compacts. Where CI exists the 6-hourly sweep does the amortized work. Neither
path holds the store lock across anything a person or agent waits on.

## What this ticket actually taught, beyond the code

The original bug I was sent to fix did not exist. `sunlit-cynical-ray` asserted the close held
the lock across the LLM completion verifier; three independent proofs showed it never had, and
the 13m53s hold was compact-on-close, three seconds after the verifier's own commit. Everything
above followed from disproving the premise rather than implementing it.

Then the fix moved the problem twice more before it was actually fixed: removing compaction
from close left CI-less stores with no trigger at all (caught by the operator, not by me), and
the sweep that replaced it walked git history per ticket under the lock — bug 7084 recurring
one scale up, and in deployment worse than that, falling through to per-EVENT wildcard walks.
Each fix was correct and each exposed the next layer.

The review gates earned their keep, repeatedly and specifically. Across six review rounds they
caught: a path-keyed map that would have missed every lookup and silently restored the
per-event walks; an empty-dict fallback strictly worse than the bug, with my own comment
asserting the opposite; a dry-run that performed a real push; a convergence test that never
merged; and three separate vacuous assertions of mine. The two classes a passing suite cannot
catch — a plausible-looking wrong primitive, and a test that cannot fail — are exactly the two
I shipped repeatedly.

## Left open deliberately

`camerashy-erectable-frog` — a blocked writer sees only a bare pid in `flock: could not acquire
lock`, with nothing indicating the holder is optional housekeeping that is safe to interrupt.
The guarantee already exists in `run_sweep`'s docstring and never reaches the operator; it cost
another lane 24 minutes and forced a manual kill of a 26-minute sweep. Filed with a full plan
rather than folded into a change that was already at +1.
